First Ireland cricketer to be sold at WPL auction 
 Edited by Nitesh Dubey / TIMESOFINDIA.COM / Oct 28, 2026, 19:23 IST Save Comments Share Aa + Text Size Small
 Medium
 Large
 Print Ireland’s seam-bowling all-rounder Orla Prendergast (Image: IANS) Ireland all-rounder Orla Prendergast has created history at the Women's Premier League (WPL) 2027 auction, becoming the first player from her country to secure a contract in the tournament. Gujarat Giants signed the 24-year-old for her base price of Rs 30 lakh at the auction in Kochi. Watch Bhuvneshwar Kumar press conference: Abhishek Sharma's fearless batting, T20 mindset and more Who is Orla Prendergast? 
 Born on June 1, 2002, in Dublin, Ireland, Prendergast is a right-handed batter who bowls right-arm medium-fast. She made her T20 International debut against the Netherlands in August 2019 and went on to make her ODI debut in October 2021. Orla Prendergast's international career and statistics Prendergast's numbers underline her value as a genuine all-rounder. She has made significant contributions in both white-ball formats.  Her performances with both bat and ball have established her as one of Ireland's key players in international cricket. ICC recognition and rise in international cricket 
 Prendergast's progress has also earned international recognition. In September 2025, she was named the ICC Women's Player of the Month for August after a series of impactful performances for Ireland. She scored 144 runs and took four wickets in Ireland's T20I series against Pakistan, which Ireland won 2-1. She followed that up with 244 runs and seven wickets during the ICC Women's T20 World Cup Europe Qualifier, further highlighting her ability to influence matches in multiple departments. From football to cricket 
 Prendergast's sporting journey began beyond the cricket field. As a youngster, she represented the Republic of Ireland at under-17 level in football and played club football for Cabinteely FC. She eventually chose cricket as her professional pathway, a decision that has since paid dividends through her rise in international cricket.
